title: Cold & Flu Relief

drivers.name: Price increase (6.2%)
drivers.evidence: At same price ($12.03), sales were 13 and 24 (vs baseline 18.5); median 1.3 vs baseline. Noise-adjusted estimate suggests weak negative effect. No past promotion at this price.

drivers.name: Heatwave (38°C)
drivers.evidence: No historical evidence linking extreme heat to cold & flu sales. No past heatwave with similar data. Not a known driver.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 18.5. No events or promotions are scheduled. The price is 6.2% above regular, which historically has not been tested in this product's past. Recent weeks show no price effect: at $12.03, sales were 13 and 24 units (vs baseline 18.5), suggesting a small negative impact. The heatwave (38°C) may drive demand for cold & flu relief if it correlates with illness, but no such link is supported by historical data. The classical uplift model suggests no effect, and evidence is thin. Shrink toward 1.0. No driver justifies a meaningful move. Uncertainty remains high.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 18.5 | 5%-95%: 1.4 - 40.9 | 10%-90%: 5.8 - 35.9

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-46% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
